title: Fleet slimming and slot-saturation mapper for Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Build a lightweight analysis and action engine that maps per-tenant slot saturation, recommends shrink/expand actions, and surfaces safe autoscale policy edits to reduce committed spend while preserving throughput SLOs.
description: Problem: Dedicated customers are often over-committed due to conservative rules-of-thumb and historical peak reservations. This drives unnecessary monthly cost and reduces capacity available for other tenants. Goal: implement a 'Fleet Slimming and Slot-Saturation Mapper' that ingests pool telemetry, per-tenant request distributions, latency SLOs and committed slab economics to generate prescriptive actions: safe shrink candidates, buffer sizing, and autoscale policy adjustments. The system should produce human-readable recommendations, a confidence score, and an audit trail for any automated or manual changes. Outcome: measurable reduction in committed GPU hours for customers that opt into recommendations, with minimal SLO regressions and clear rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry sidecar exports per-pool slot utilization and kernel-level saturation at 1m granularity
Algorithm identifies shrink candidates with estimated risk and potential monthly cost savings
UI/console view listing recommended actions with explainability and links to affected pools
A/B test run for 5 pilot customers showing <=5% SLO violations and >=12% committed-hour reduction for opt-in cases
Automated guardrails block any recommendation that would reduce capacity below configured safety-buffer
implementation_plan: Instrument: add slot-saturation metrics to existing pool exporter (slot_busy_ratio, avg_batch_size, tail_latency_p95)
Aggregate: new downward-sampled indexes in telemetry pipeline for 1h and 24h patterns
Analyze: implement saturation mapper service that computes candidate deltas and simulates autoscale policy edits against historical traces
Surface: backend API and Console panel with recommendations, confidence, and simulation preview
Pilot: run as read-only recommendations for first week, then offer opt-in automated apply for pilot customers
Monitor: roll out alerts and dashboards to detect SLO regressions and automated rollback triggers
metrics_to_track: SLO violation rate (p95 latency) for impacted routes
Monthly cost savings estimate aggregated across pilots
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive shrink leads to tail latency regressions. Mitigation: require simulation pass and 'safety_buffer' config; block any action that raises predicted p95 beyond configured SLO
Risk: telemetry noise produces false positives. Mitigation: require 7-day minimum data and seasonal-aware smoothing; mark low-confidence recommendations as advisory only
Risk: customer mistrust of automated changes. Mitigation: default to opt-in; provide clear audit trail and rollback button; include human-readable explanation of why recommendation is safe
Risk: edge-case with heterogenous workloads (burst + long-tail). Mitigation: tag tenants with workload archetype and run separate heuristics per archetype
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dedicated-fleet-slimming (internal) — includes sim strategy and API contract
Decision: start with read-only recommendations for 30 days before enabling any automated apply — approved by PM and Security on 2026-02-25
